packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no identification was revealed to me by prior context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only) - begun from image-001 (overview) and image-002 (tile)
image-001 is a reduced overview: a bound volume lying open/flat with its spine
area exposed, a steel rule (cm) and a colour checker below. In the gap of the
spine two pieces of written parchment are visible in situ as spine linings /
binding strips (tentative interpretation of function), each c. 5-6 cm wide on
the rule: a LEFT piece (at c. 21.5-27 cm on the rule) carrying a red letter,
and a RIGHT piece (at c. 13-19 cm) with several lines of dark script. Each
piece continues below a tear/fold as a lower flap partly covered by the
volume's white covering material. The script on the strips runs horizontally
in the photograph as far as can be seen. The pieces are creased, darkened and
abraded; no column structure, running title or gloss can be made out at this
scale.

image-002 (native tile of the LEFT piece, upper part)
Observations: one red enlarged initial or paraph-like letter, a tall shaft
with a flag at top and a long foot serif - shape of a capital "I" (c. 3 text
lines high). Left of it, several lines of very faint, abraded dark script
(line-ends running up to the initial's left); right of it the surface is
mostly blank/abraded except for a later-looking larger cursive scrawl at lower
right. I count about six faint line-levels left of the initial.
image-002 line 1: [illegible; a V-shaped dark mark at far upper left, possibly a letter or a stain]
image-002 line 2: [illegible] ...i i c(?)[  then red initial "I"
image-002 line 3: [illegible traces]
image-002 line 4: ]u(?)m(?)... [minims: "ui m"/"num"?] [illegible] .
image-002 line 5: ]o(?)d(?)o(?) [illegible minims] ...   [a row of round letters at far left, "oro"/"ore"/"ddo"?; rest abraded]
image-002 line 6: [illegible traces]
image-002 right side, later scrawl: "9 r 2n"? / "g... Zu"?  [large cursive strokes, not read]

image-003 (second reduced overview)
The same volume photographed turned through 180 degrees (rule and colour
checker now above; the red-letter piece now on the right, at c. 20-26 cm, the
dark-script piece on the left, at c. 13-18.5 cm). In this view the flaps that
lie against the upper board show a few lines of brownish script (above the
dark-script piece) and, above the red-letter piece, a pale flap with faint
script at its upper edge. The red letter appears upside down relative to
image-001, so one of the two overviews shows the strips inverted; from the
letter-forms in the tiles, image-003/-004 show the dark script the right way up
(tentative).

image-004 (native tile: the dark-script piece as seen in image-003, with the lighter flap above it)
Observations: two zones. UPPER ZONE (lighter, yellowish flap, partly covered at
upper left by white torn covering material): four line-levels of brown
script, faded, in what looks like a more cursive/smaller hand or possibly
an offset - I cannot decide. LOWER ZONE (dark brown, cockled, on the spine
itself): about seven line-levels of a heavier, upright gothic book hand in
black-brown ink; only the right-hand part of each line (c. 3-4 cm) is
exposed, the left being abraded. The right edge is a cut/torn edge against
the black gap. No red, initial, or ruling seen in this tile.
UPPER ZONE
image-004 line 1: ]be(?) . diuio(?) . [illegible]      (letters brown, tops under the white cover; "diuio"/"dixito"/"bisto" all possible)
image-004 line 2: ]ecu(n)d(?) . l(?) nus(?) yas(?)[      ("...tur. l mis ipās"? a group ending in a "-us"/"-is" and a final word with a y- or long-descender letter and abbreviation stroke)
image-004 line 3: [covered by white fibres at left] ]rub(?) / ]mb(us)? sine(?) / s(u)nt(?)[   (a word ending in "b" with tall ascender, then a word beginning with long s)
image-004 line 4: [illegible traces] ... l(?)[
(horizontal fold/crease; a single upright stroke "I"/"l" stands on it at mid-width)
LOWER ZONE
image-004 line 5: [dark, abraded; tops of letters only] ...e(?) a(?) . ll(?)[
image-004 line 6: A(?)e... c(?)illas(?) / ...ullas(?) [illegible]      (a larger letter at far left like "A"/"d"; then abraded; a group "-illas"/"-ulias"/"-nitas" near centre)
image-004 line 7: viuat(?) / uiuat(?) / unitas(?) p(ro)?[      (group of minims + "a" + tall final letter: "uiuat"/"uniat"/"inuiat"/"mutat"; then "p" with a looped/abbreviated bowl and a round letter at the edge: "p(ro)"/"po")
image-004 line 8: le(?) . l . i . l . o(?)[      (short upright strokes separated by points - reads like a string of single letters or numerals with points, e.g. ". l . i . l ."/". i . ii ."; first sign like "k"/"le"/"R"; last a round letter)
image-004 line 9: ligna(?) / signa(?) / lingua(?) - m(?)[      (tall first letter "l"/long "s" with a loop, then "igna"/"ingua", a dash-like stroke, then minims at the edge)
image-004 line 10: [X-shaped mark or crossed letter at far left] ...u(?) ... ibo(?) . / bo(n)a(?) .      (right-hand group "ibo"/"bro"/"vbo" followed by a point)
image-004 line 11: ...c(?)i(?) . ilia(?) / . ulla(?) / . itia[      (after a point, minims + "a")
image-004 line 12: [bottom edge; tops of letters "e"/"o"... illegible]

image-005 (third reduced overview)
Same orientation as image-003, but a hand with tweezers lifts the white
covering material at the board edge, exposing more of the lighter flap above
the dark-script piece (about four to five brown lines now visible there) and
the pale flap above the red-letter piece (faint lines along its right half).

image-006 (native tile; OVERLAPS image-004 - same piece, same lower zone, with one more line of the upper zone exposed by the lifting)
The lower zone repeats image-004 lines 5-12 and is not additional text. Upper zone as seen here:
image-006 line 1: ]i..o(?) [illegible] ...a(?) .      (faint; a group at left and a single "a"/"g"-like letter with a point at far right)
image-006 line 2: (v?)o(?)diuio(?) . i(?)[      (= image-004 line 1, now with its beginning: first sign like a "v"/"r" with a hooked stroke, then "odiuio"/"odnio"/"adiuto"; a point; a minim at the edge)
image-006 line 3: eur(?) . l mis(?) yas(?) / ipas(?)[      (= image-004 line 2: "cur"/"eur"/"tur", point, tall "l" or "I", "mis"/"nus"/"rius", then a word with y-like first letter and abbreviation stroke above)
image-006 line 4: [white fibres] ...rub(?) / ...mb(?) me(?) / ine(?)[      (= image-004 line 3; a tall flourished letter rises above the group before "b")
image-006 line 5: [traces at the fold] ...l . [illegible]
Lower zone (repeat of image-004, slightly clearer here):
image-006 line 6: [abraded] ...ij(?)... e(?)[
image-006 line 7: A(?)[illegible] ...ti(?)... o(?)u(?)[      (large first letter "A"/"d" at left)
image-006 line 8: [illegible] ...mas(?) / ...illas(?)
image-006 line 9: viuat(?) / uniat(?) p(ro)?[      (as image-004 line 7; a horizontal stroke runs under-left of the first letter)
image-006 line 10: k(?)/le . l . i . l . o(?)[      (as image-004 line 8)
image-006 line 11: ligna(?) / signa(?) - [illegible]      (as image-004 line 9)
image-006 line 12: [X-like mark at left] ... i(?) ... ibo(?) .
image-006 line 13: ...ati(?) . ilia(?) / ulla(?)
image-006 line 14: ...e(?)lo(?)...  [letters cut by lower edge]
image-006 line 15: [bottom: a further line partly visible, "...rat(?)..." - illegible]

image-007 (fourth reduced overview)
Same orientation as image-001, with tweezers lifting the white covering
material below the dark-script piece: the lower flap of that piece now shows
about four lines of brown script (the same lighter zone as in image-004/-006,
here seen from the other direction, i.e. upside down relative to image-006).
The red-letter piece and its lower flap (faint lines on the flap's left half)
are as in image-001.

image-008 (native tile; OVERLAPS image-002 - the red-letter piece, same view, marginally sharper)
Not additional text. Readings as far as I can take them:
image-008 line 1: [dark V-shaped mark / "vi"? at far upper left on the bulge; illegible]
image-008 line 2: [illegible] ... i i i(?) c(?) / o(?)   then the red initial "I" begins (a small red tick stands above the last black letter)
image-008 line 3: [illegible traces] ... l(?) ... ti(?)
image-008 line 4: ]u . i u(?)m(?) e(?)... [illegible] .      (heavy minims: "n.i ni e"/"uiuu(m)"? then abraded letters up to a hole)
image-008 line 5: ]oio(?) / ]ore(?) / ]dio(?) . m(?)...x(?)... [illegible]      (round letters at the far left edge, then a point, then abraded minims)
image-008 line 6: [illegible traces] ... n(?)
image-008 line 7: [illegible traces]
Red: initial "I", c. 3 lines high, standing to the RIGHT of these line-ends;
no text is visible to its right apart from the later scrawl ("9 r 2n"?/"G.. Zy"?).
Tentative interpretation: either the initial opens a column whose text is lost
to abrasion on the right, or this view is inverted and the initial's text lies
on the other side; I could not settle the orientation of this piece from the
letter-forms.

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
All eight images were viewed (four overviews: 001, 003, 005, 007; four tiles:
002, 004, 006, 008). Tiles 004 and 006 show the same piece and overlap almost
entirely; tiles 002 and 008 show the same piece and overlap almost entirely.
I attempted every visible line on both pieces. No span of connected, checkable
text resulted: the best is the right-hand ends of about eight lines on the
dark-script piece (image-006 lines 7-14), where individual letter groups can be
seen but word readings stay uncertain ("uiuat"? "p(ro)"? "ligna/signa"?
"...ibo."? ". ilia"?, and a line that looks like single letters or numerals
separated by points). NOT read at all: the pale flap adjoining the red-letter
piece (visible in overviews 001/003/005/007 only at reduced scale, with faint
lines), and the lighter flap of the dark-script piece as seen in image-007
(no tile supplied for that view).

LIMITATIONS
- The fragments are in situ in a binding, cockled, darkened and abraded; large parts of every line are hidden under the covering material or lost.
- Orientation is uncertain: the overviews show the volume in two opposite orientations. I read the dark-script piece in the orientation of image-004/-006, where the letter-forms look upright; the red-letter piece was read as shown in image-002/-008 and may be inverted.
- The lighter upper zone (image-004 lines 1-4 / image-006 lines 1-5) may be a different hand from the dark lower zone, or the same hand less darkened, or an offset; undecided.
- Readings marked with "?" are letter-shape guesses, not word readings; nothing here should be treated as a secure transcription.
- Useful additions: a native-resolution tile of the pale flap next to the red-letter piece; a tile of the newly exposed lines in image-007; multispectral or raking-light images of the dark piece; and images after the strips are lifted, if conservation allows.
- I did nothing beyond the rules: opened only PROMPT.md and the eight image files of this packet.
